text: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying:

versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses both וַיְדַבֵּר (spoke) and לֵאמֹר (saying); rendering it as 'spoke to Moses' better matches the formula used elsewhere, though the shorter form is acceptable for oral flow.

text: Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites, and say to them: This is what the LORD has commanded:
Anyone from the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat inside the camp, or slaughters it outside the camp,

versions.text: Any Israelite who slaughters an ox, a lamb, or a goat inside the camp, or outside the camp,
versions.explanation: The idiom 'from the house of Israel' is rendered literally in verses 8 and 10 but flattened here; consistency helps oral hearers. Also the second clause repeats the verb in Hebrew ('or who slaughters it outside the camp').

text: instead of bringing it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD before the LORD's dwelling—that man shall be held guilty of bloodshed. He has shed blood, and he shall be cut off from among his people.

This is so that the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been offering out in the open field. They must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrifice them as peace offerings to the LORD.

versions.text: This is so that the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices they have been offering out in the open field. They must bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrifice them there as fellowship offerings to the LORD.
versions.explanation: 'Fellowship offerings' is an interpretive rendering of זִבְחֵי שְׁלָמִים; 'peace offerings' is closer to the Hebrew root and consistent with common usage in Leviticus. The added 'there' is not in the Hebrew.

text: The priest shall splash the blood against the altar of the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat demons, after whom they prostitute themselves. This shall be a lasting statute for them through all their generations.
Say to them: Anyone from the house of Israel, or any foreigner residing among them, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD—that man shall be cut off from his people.
If anyone from the house of Israel, or any foreigner residing among them, eats any blood, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives; for it is the blood that makes atonement by means of the life.

versions.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your souls; for it is the blood that makes atonement by means of the life.
versions.explanation: נַפְשֹׁתֵיכֶם is the same word (nephesh) translated 'life' earlier in the verse; using 'souls' here introduces an inconsistency and a body/soul dualism not present in the Hebrew. 'Lives' keeps the wordplay clear for hearers.

text: That is why I have said to the Israelites: None of you may eat blood, nor may any foreigner residing among you eat blood.
Anyone among the Israelites, or any foreigner residing among them, who hunts and catches an animal or a bird that may be eaten must drain out its blood and cover it with earth.

For the life of every creature is in its blood. Therefore I said to the Israelites: You must not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.

versions.text: For the life of every creature is its blood; its blood is its life. That is why I have said to the Israelites: You must not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood. Whoever eats it shall be cut off.
versions.explanation: The opening clause is rendered twice ('its blood is its life') which duplicates content not doubled in the Hebrew, making the verse wordy for oral reading. Also 'That is why' opens verse 12 identically; varying to 'Therefore' avoids monotony.

text: Anyone, whether native-born or foreigner, who eats an animal found dead or torn by wild beasts must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening; then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes and bathe himself, he will bear his guilt.
